properties.decision:
SETTLED BY ANTHONY, 2026-09-28, verbatim: "how is the question 'should reflow2 serve a design that is already in operations?' not already answered? I've designed reflow2 from the beginning to be the complete lifecycle from concept to operations/fielding. One of the core principles of reflow2 is that design doesn't drift from implementation. We've even compared this to UAF, which also captures the full life-cycle ... the answer, in my mind, is very clearly yes. Secondly, many coding projects live in a continuous development, continuous integration - this means that many projects are never fully and completely integrated. For many projects, there is a near continuous cycle to iterative deployment, testing, feedback, operations that sticks around for years. In coding this is very evident. In other domains, look at the B-52. It's maiden flight was on April 15, 1952 and Extended Service Life: Comprehensive avionics, communication, and structural overhauls mean the B-52J will keep the aircraft flying into the 2050s and 2060s."

WHAT WAS ALREADY WRITTEN, and why this node should never have been framed as open:
· docs/vision.md, since the first commit (2026-07-17): "one coherent graph from concept to operations". It names build → operate as a transition where programs break, and "concept, design, build, test, production, O&M" as the phases. Its definition of good: "Someone with only an idea is guided — by questions — from concept to operations without needing to know systems engineering."
· req:coherence (accepted, critical): the design stays coherent across its lifecycle, in any phase.
· req:design-and-implementation-stay-coherent-both-ways (accepted 2026-09-25): changes the implementation forces, from testing or any other feedback, are reflected back into the design, physical implementations included.
The agent that first wrote this node framed it as OPEN, with "beside the design" and "nothing new" as options. That was wrong, and it is root-caused in fact:root-cause-the-lifecycle-scope-lives-in-the-vision-and-the-graph-holds-one-line-so-a-brainstorm-reopened-it-2026-09-28. The earlier text is kept in the revision snapshot.

WHAT THIS SETTLES:
· Operations is inside reflow2's core, not a new feature family. An incident, the evidence gathered, the cause found and the fix made are the implementation feeding back into the design, which req:design-and-implementation-stay-coherent-both-ways already requires.
· The lifecycle is a LOOP, not a line. Deploy, test, feed back, operate and change repeat for as long as the system lives: years for a codebase under continuous delivery, a century for an airframe. The design is never "done" and handed off.

WHAT IT DOES NOT SETTLE, left open in the ideas beside it, from the hxm_program report (art:hxm-program-feedback-2026-09-28):
· how an incident is recorded cheaply on an asset the design has not modelled yet (O-17);
· how precedent search reaches the file archive (O-18);
· how operator evidence closes a stale check (O-19);
· how the loop ranks an operating project's signal (O-20);
· how the physical plant is adopted (O-21).
Those are HOW questions, and the counter-arguments recorded on each (mature tools exist, cost, the fewer-things advice) weigh the how, never the whether.

WHAT THE REPORT MEASURED stays true and is now read as a gap against settled intent, not as a question of scope. About a fifth of an operations day touched the graph. 8 changed files went unreconciled. One incident produced zero design nodes. The same triage found that the loop's order is fixed for the design phase and a project cannot declare it is operating (fact:root-cause-the-loops-order-is-fixed-for-the-design-phase-and-the-operations-signal-is-not-in-it-2026-09-28).

2026-09-28, LATER THE SAME DAY, Anthony: "one of the very reasons that I created epochs/increments into reflow2 was because many designs continue development and operations simultaneously in sort of an iterative or incremental deployment of capabilities. That is also in the reflow2 graph." It is: req:epochs-can-be-planned (accepted) has "increments in CAPABILITY — what each small, frequent release adds". The readiness gate distinguishes a demonstrator from a fielded increment. The as-fielded reconcile (cap:reconcile-deployed) checks deployed releases against what is running. So the loop settled above is already modelled. An operating increment and the next increment in development are two positions on one design's time axis, not two phases of a project.
properties.name: SETTLED 2026-09-28, and settled since the first commit: reflow2 serves a design for its whole life, concept → operations, and for most systems that life is a loop that runs for years. What remains open is HOW operations evidence reaches the design (the ideas beside this node)
properties.rationale: First written 2026-09-28 as an exploratory OPEN question during the triage of the hxm_program report. Rewritten the same day on Anthony's word, because the question was already answered by the vision and by two accepted requirements. The node is kept, not deleted, so the misframing and its root cause stay findable, and the child ideas keep the node they point at.
